do_more: Use specific references to classic psychology books or theories in the hook
Pose a direct, curiosity‑driven question in the title
Keep the script tight (~30 s) for fast‑consumption or a standard ~42 s for deeper dive
Start with a strong visual cue (e.g., book cover or illustration) and a clear narrative arc
Focus on surprising or counter‑intuitive facts that boost watch‑through rate
avoid: Generic, emoji‑filled titles without a clear hook
Overly broad questions that lack a concrete answer
Videos longer than 45 s that lose audience attention
Click‑bait phrasing without delivering substantive content
short.title_style: Start with a concrete hook or question, cite a classic work, and promise a surprising insight in under 8 words
next_tests: Release paired versions of the same script at 30 s and 42 s to compare VPD
Swap question‑based titles for statement‑based titles to see impact on avg watch %
Add a brief on‑screen book‑cover intro vs plain background to test visual hook
short.best_title: The Expression of the Emotions in Man and Animals · Watching expression · Reading 5

do_more: Start videos with a concrete, surprising hook about a specific psychological phenomenon (e.g., "Why crowds whisper secrets"),
Label each episode as part of a series (e.g., "Guided reading" or "Reading X") in the title and intro,
Mention a well‑known researcher or historical figure when relevant to add authority,
Keep the opening hook tight (~30 s) before moving into the main content
avoid: Broad, generic questions without a clear angle (e.g., "What does psychoanalysis say?"),
Long, unfocused intros that delay the hook,
Titles that lack series tags or a specific hook phrase
full.title_style: Use a clear, curiosity‑driving hook followed by a concrete topic and series label, e.g., "Why crowds whisper secrets | Guided reading · Reading 2"
next_tests: A/B test titles with and without the "Guided reading" tag to see impact on VPD
Create two versions of each video: one with a 30‑second hook and one with a 45‑second hook, compare performance
Add a historical figure’s name to half the titles (e.g., "Gustave Le Bon") and measure view‑per‑day changes
